data.title: Text Truncate
data.tagline: Shorten text that cannot fit in the available space
data.description: Text truncation keeps a title or filename from breaking a compact layout, usually with an ellipsis. It hides information, so provide the full value when people may need it. Decide whether the limit is one line, several lines, or a fixed character count.

use: Long filename in a compact row
Card title with a fixed height
Preview text where the full value is available elsewhere
avoid: Cut off text that people must read to decide
Truncate without any way to see the full value
Use character limits when layout width is the real constraint
Apply the same line limit to every type of content

lessonPractice.title: An order table has limited product-title width, but price and status must always remain complete. How should long content be handled?

options.label: Truncate only the title with an ellipsis and provide a full-text path usable by keyboard and touch
options.feedback: The title can shorten in a limited column while remaining accessible, and decision-critical price and status stay complete.

options.label: Truncate title, price, and status to one line so every column has identical width
options.feedback: Price and status are required for the order judgment, and hiding them can prevent confirmation.

options.label: Ellipsize long titles, keep the full value only in API data, and provide no viewing path
options.feedback: The ellipsis only signals hidden content. Without an outlet, users can never access the missing part.

data.agentPrompt: Ellipsize product titles within the limited order-table column while keeping price, date, and status complete. Provide a focusable, touch-accessible way to view or copy the full title, and verify min-width and overflow inside Flex or Grid.
